universities.name: Medical University of Warsaw
universities.summary: Medical University of Warsaw is one of Poland's largest medical universities, with a continuous medical teaching tradition dating to 1809. Its English Division, established in 1993, runs a direct-entry, six-year MD programme listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools, awarding the Polish Lekarz qualification with EU Directive 2005/36/EC automatic recognition across the EU and EEA.
universities.campusLifestyle: The Faculty of Medicine educates over 4,500 students across its six-year programme in all languages, with roughly 700 English Division students currently enrolled from more than 75 countries. Facilities include the Didactic Center, Banacha and Lindleya campuses, a Medical Simulation Centre, over 100 student associations (15 conducted in English) and more than 80 optional courses (25 in English).
universities.cityProfile: Warsaw, Poland's capital and largest city, hosts Medical University of Warsaw's Faculty of Medicine. International students are supported by the English Division Student Government, which organizes Orientation Week and ongoing community activities, alongside a peer Mentor-Mentee programme run jointly with IFMSA and active chapters of IFMSA and the European Medical Students' Association.
universities.practicalExposure: The six-year, 384-ECTS curriculum runs roughly three pre-clinical years followed by three years with a growing share of clinical training, plus a mandatory 20 weeks of summer clerkship spread across the programme; clinical training makes up 50-74% of the full curriculum per the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools. Clinical instruction takes place at the university's own teaching hospitals -- the Independent Public Central Clinical Hospital, Jozef Polikarp Brudzinski Public Pediatric Clinical Hospital, Infant Jesus Clinical Hospital, Duchess Anna Mazowiecka Hospital, the Independent Public Clinical Ophthalmology Hospital, the University Dental Center and the University Centre of Mother and Child's Health -- plus a dedicated Medical Simulation Centre. Graduates receive the Polish Lekarz qualification, which carries EU-wide automatic recognition once the Lekarski Egzamin Koncowy final exam and a postgraduate internship are also completed.
universities.hostelOverview: The university's Student Dormitory No. 2 BIS in the Wola district offers a limited, first-come-first-served number of places to first-year English Division students. For 2026-27, rates run EUR 2,738 per semester for a single room with private bathroom, or EUR 1,370 per semester for a shared double room, plus a deposit. Students who do not secure a university place can use the university's accredited private-partner dormitories in the Mokotow district.
universities.dietarySupport: No specific on-campus meal plan or dining-cost figure is published. Community kitchens are available on each dormitory floor, but kitchen appliances are not permitted in individual rooms. Daily food costs should be planned as a separate budget line alongside tuition and accommodation.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found for the Faculty of Medicine. International students can reach the English Division Student Government and an Ombudsman office for support with any concerns.
universities.studentSupport: The English Division Student Government organizes Orientation Week and a peer Mentor-Mentee programme with IFMSA. Additional administrative support runs through a Virtual Dean's Office and Student Inbox, alongside active IFMSA and European Medical Students' Association chapters.
whyChoose: A continuous medical teaching tradition dating to 1809, with an English Division running since 1993 and roughly 700 international students currently enrolled from more than 75 countries.
Listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools, with graduates noted as ECFMG-certification eligible for graduation years 1953 onward, subject to standard requirements.
The Polish Lekarz qualification carries EU Directive 2005/36/EC automatic recognition across the EU and EEA once the final licensing exam and postgraduate internship are completed.
Clinical training spans multiple named university-run teaching hospitals plus a dedicated Medical Simulation Centre.
A detailed, transparent multi-step admissions process with several qualifying routes: a university Competency Test, recognized standardized test scores, or university GPA for degree-holders.
thingsToConsider: Total programme cost is substantial: EUR 112,800 tuition over six years (EUR 18,800 per year for the 2026-27 cohort), plus a non-refundable EUR 1,000 confirmation fee (only EUR 500 refundable if withdrawing in writing before 15 July) and a separate application fee.

A 2025 Polish law change tightened exemptions from the university's own Competency Test -- most standardized-test-score holders and bachelor's or master's degree holders are no longer automatically exempt and need individual Admission Board confirmation before applying via those routes.
University-dormitory placement for first-year students is limited and first-come-first-served; many students will need private accommodation at additional cost.
Indian applicants must separately satisfy India's National Medical Commission NEET-UG Eligibility Certificate requirement; this is not referenced or administered by the university.
bestFitFor: Students able to fund a premium EU medical degree without requiring the Polish-language track, and strong in Biology and Chemistry for the Competency Test.
Applicants who prioritize EU-wide licence recognition over a faster or lower-cost non-EU pathway.
Families comfortable navigating a detailed, multi-step Polish admissions process, including bank-transfer-only EUR payments and case-by-case exemption confirmations.

faq.question: Is the Medicine programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. Polish law classifies it as a long-cycle Master's programme, but it is direct-entry: admission follows straight from secondary education with no separate bachelor's stage.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive a Polish medical diploma with the degree title Lekarz, listed under EU Directive 2005/36/EC for automatic recognition across the EU/EEA once the Lekarski Egzamin Koncowy final exam and a postgraduate internship are also completed.

faq.question: How long is the programme and how is it structured?
faq.answer: Six years (384 ECTS credits): roughly three pre-clinical years followed by three years with a growing share of clinical training, plus a mandatory 20 weeks of summer clerkship spread across the years.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: For the 2026-27 academic year, tuition is EUR 18,800 per year (EUR 112,800 for the full six-year course), payable in two or four instalments per year.

faq.question: Are there additional fees besides tuition?
faq.answer: Yes -- a non-refundable application fee and a non-refundable EUR 1,000 confirmation fee, of which only EUR 500 is refundable if a candidate withdraws in writing before 15 July.

faq.question: What entrance exam does the university require?
faq.answer: The default route is the university's own Competency Test: 80 questions covering Biology, Chemistry and Decision Making. Candidates may alternatively submit a qualifying standardized test score or, for bachelor's or master's degree holders, a qualifying GPA, though a 2025 law change means most candidates in these alternate routes need individual confirmation from the Admission Board.

faq.question: When does the academic year start?
faq.answer: The academic year begins with Orientation Week, provisionally scheduled for the last week of September, with the final schedule published each September.

faq.question: Is the English Division open to Polish citizens?
faq.answer: No. The English-taught six-year Medicine programme is restricted to non-citizens of Poland.

faq.question: Do Indian students need NEET to join this programme?
faq.answer: The university's own admissions criteria do not reference NEET. Separately, India's National Medical Commission requires Indian citizens and OCI holders who obtain a primary medical qualification abroad to have qualified NEET-UG, whose result serves as the mandatory Eligibility Certificate.

faq.question: What accommodation options exist for first-year students?
faq.answer: The university's own Student Dormitory No. 2 BIS offers a limited, first-come-first-served number of places to first-year English Division students; those who don't secure a place can use accredited private partner dormitories.

fee.notes: Officially published under Rector's Order No. 58/2026 (25 February 2026): EUR 18,800 per year, EUR 112,800 total for the six-year course, payable in 2 instalments of EUR 9,600 or 4 instalments of EUR 4,900. Separate charges apply: a non-refundable application fee (EUR 20-24 depending on recruitment route) and a non-refundable EUR 1,000 Start-up/Confirmation Fee, credited toward tuition (only EUR 500 refundable if withdrawal is filed in writing before 15 July 2026).

eligibleAudiences: International (non-Polish-citizen) applicants holding a secondary-education diploma, IB Diploma or new Polish maturity certificate
Bachelor's or master's degree holders and recognized standardized-test-score holders, subject to individual Admission Board confirmation of exemption eligibility
restrictions: The English Division programme is restricted to non-citizens of Poland
Indian applicants must separately hold a current NEET-UG qualification under India's National Medical Commission rules; this is not administered by the university itself
audienceEligibility.notes: A 2025 Polish law change (Act of 4 April 2025) tightened exemptions from the university's own Competency Test; most standardized-test-score and degree-holder candidates now need individual pre-confirmation from the Admission Board.

admissionsContent.overview: Applicants choose a recruitment path (Competency Test, standardized test score, or GPA for degree holders), apply through the Online Registration System, pay the application fee, and are ranked on secondary-school grades plus their Criterion 2 qualification (test, score, or GPA).

eligibility.intro: Applicants need a secondary-education diploma (or IB/EB/Polish maturity equivalent) with required-subject grades, English proficiency, and a passing Criterion 2 qualification via the Competency Test, a recognized standardized test score, or GPA for degree holders.
items: Secondary school-leaving certificate or equivalent (IB Geneva, EB Brussels, or Polish maturity certificate)
Passing grades in required subjects, or a supplementary WUM entrance exam for any missing subject (minimum 30%, up to two subjects)

Competency Test (80 questions: Biology, Chemistry, Decision Making), OR a qualifying UCAT/BMAT/MCAT/GAMSAT/HPAT score, OR university GPA for BSc/MSc holders -- each subject to 2025 exemption-confirmation rules
Indian applicants: current NEET-UG qualification per India's National Medical Commission rules, separate from the university's own admission process

applicationSteps: Choose the correct recruitment path and, if applicable, email document scans to the Admission Board for pre-confirmation
Apply online via the Online Registration System (ORS), selecting the application type matching the chosen path
Pay the non-refundable application fee by bank transfer
Complete Criterion 2 qualification: sit the Competency Test, or present a qualifying test score or GPA
If accepted, pay the non-refundable Start-up Fee for Tuition and complete the remaining Admission File before Orientation Week

academic: Secondary school-leaving certificate/diploma with transcripts, or predicted grades for current-year graduates
For the GPA route: BSc or MSc diploma with official transcript and grading-scale explanation
application: Certified translations into English or Polish where required

admissionsContent.deadlinesNote: 2026-27 intake: online registration closes 30 June 2026, competency-test qualification deadline 1 July 2026, confirmation-fee partial-refund deadline 15 July 2026, Orientation Week provisionally 28-30 September 2026.
visaConsiderations: Confirm current Polish student-visa and residency requirements directly with the university, given recent immigration-law changes affecting foreign-student admission.
